items.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: Buddy Collette and his Friends playing those arrangements.

ctx.x: Well at the time most people thought if a tuba was going to be in jazz then it would be old timey, perhaps early New Orleans music with a bomp-bomp-bomp type thing going on. There wasn’t too many role models other than that for you to listen to, was there?

No but I was interested in anybody playing the tuba you know, whether it be Red Callender, the great bass player, who also in the 50s, in ’54, put out a couple of jazz LPs with a rhythm section and Buddy Collette and his Friends playing those arrangements.
Oh right, on the west coast.
